candidates.name: Orthodox Church of Ukraine worship activity in Austria
candidates.reason: The official OCU report documents a January 2025 visit and worship with the Ecumenical Patriarchate in its Holy Trinity Cathedral in Vienna. It does not identify a separate permanent OCU parish, mission, chapel, monastery, metochion or recurring worship site. Retain until the OCU publishes a stable Austrian body.

candidates.name: Macedonian Orthodox church community in Villach
candidates.claimed_parent: European Diocese of the Macedonian Orthodox Church
candidates.reason: The current official diocese establishes Villach as one of its four Austrian church communities, so the community is published. Its dedication, address and regular schedule remain here for reconciliation because no current official page was found that publishes them.

candidates.name: Macedonian Orthodox church community in Salzburg
candidates.claimed_parent: European Diocese of the Macedonian Orthodox Church
candidates.reason: The current official diocese establishes Salzburg as its fourth Austrian church community, so the community is published. The founding report documents the first Liturgy but does not establish a dedication, permanent address or recurring schedule. Those details remain unresolved rather than being inferred from secondary listings.

candidates.name: Ukrainian Orthodox Church community in Maria Ellend
candidates.claimed_parent: Western European Vicariate of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church

superseded_or_not_current.name: St Demetrios Bulgarian Orthodox church community in Graz
superseded_or_not_current.reason: An older Bulgarian Patriarchate directory listed a St Demetrios community in Graz. The current patriarchal directory lists only the St John of Rila community and Sts Cyril and Methodius episcopal chapel in Vienna. The omitted Graz body is not published without current official confirmation.

source_reconciliation.subject: Austrian canonical jurisdiction union
source_reconciliation.result: The Orthodox Bishops Conference officially identifies seven Churches with Austrian structures: the Ecumenical Patriarchate and the Patriarchates of Antioch, Moscow, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria and Georgia. Their own current directories govern body-level coverage. Current official sources also establish ROCOR, Macedonian and UOC bodies that are preserved under their own canonical parents.

source_reconciliation.subject: Ecumenical Patriarchate coverage
source_reconciliation.result: The current Metropolis directory establishes eighteen parishes or church communities throughout Austria. Its current monastery page establishes the Protection of the Mother of God and St Paisios monastery at Sankt Andra am Zicksee. Nineteen rows are published.

source_reconciliation.subject: Serbian Orthodox coverage
source_reconciliation.result: The current diocesan East, Central and West Austria directories establish twenty primary churches or parishes and five named filial churches. All twenty-five bodies and worship sites are preserved.

source_reconciliation.subject: Romanian Orthodox coverage
source_reconciliation.result: The current Austrian parish directory, updated 15 September 2026, establishes thirty-four primary parishes or chapels and three filial churches. All thirty-seven rows are preserved under the Romanian Archdiocese of Germany, Austria and Luxembourg.

source_reconciliation.subject: Moscow Patriarchate and ROCOR coverage
source_reconciliation.result: The Vienna and Austria Diocese establishes seven current Austrian bodies. The current ROCOR German diocesan directory separately establishes the Protection church in Salzburg. The Salzburg body is preserved under ROCOR rather than duplicated under the Vienna and Austria Diocese.

source_reconciliation.subject: Antiochian, Bulgarian and Georgian coverage
source_reconciliation.result: Current official directories establish two Antiochian communities in Vienna and Hall in Tirol, two Bulgarian bodies in Vienna, and three Georgian communities in Vienna, Graz and Linz. The Georgian rows are also confirmed by the Austrian Bishops Conference's current Georgian directory.

source_reconciliation.subject: Macedonian Orthodox coverage
source_reconciliation.result: The current European Diocese identifies exactly four Austrian church communities in Vienna, Linz, Villach and Salzburg. The official older directory supplies the Vienna dedication and address. The current official sources establish the Linz dedication and the existence of the Villach and Salzburg communities. Four rows are published without inventing unresolved local details.

source_reconciliation.subject: UOC Austrian coverage
source_reconciliation.result: The current official vicariate report establishes the All Venerable Fathers of the Kyiv Caves parish in Vienna and a separate UOC community in Maria Ellend. Both are preserved under the UOC.
